title: Scholialang Skills 01: read-only cross-host version and capability Doctor
problem: Users and internal agents have encountered mismatched Scholialang Python package, scholialang-mcp package/plugin, vendored validator, grammar teaching, skill, and MCP/LSP tool versions. The current general Scholialang skill assumes installation is healthy and offers no deterministic answer to 'what is loaded, which grammar is implemented, and are these surfaces compatible?'.
outcome: The public repository contains a concise scholialang-doctor skill backed by a deterministic read-only script. It reports host, package/plugin/manifest/vendored-validator/grammar versions, MCP and LSP entry-point availability, auto-emit configuration, database reachability metadata, and compatibility as separate facets. It emits stable JSON and human output with pass, not_ready, or fail, and never installs, upgrades, authenticates, or rewrites configuration by default.
hard_constraints: Initialize the new skill with the system skill-creator init script. The canonical source must live in one repo-owned skill directory; host copies are generated artifacts and must not be hand-maintained authorities.

Keep SKILL.md concise. Put deterministic inspection in scripts/ and detailed version-axis definitions in a one-level reference only if necessary. Do not create README.md, INSTALLATION_GUIDE.md, CHANGELOG.md, or other auxiliary files inside the skill.

Doctor is read-only. It MUST NOT pip install, plugin install, upgrade, authenticate, edit config, initialize a DAG, or repair a database. Offer a separate recommendation field, never an automatic fix.

Report language grammar and package/plugin release as distinct axes. The stable Scholia grammar is v0.6.2 while the current implementation/plugin release is 0.7.2; never label that relationship as a downgrade.
Probe only public metadata and explicitly named local paths. Do not read environment secret values, credential files, DAG contents, customer data, or private reasoning.
Missing optional host surfaces are not generic failure. Return per-facet supported/present/compatible and derive an honest overall pass/not_ready/fail with reasons.
Support repository checkout inspection plus installed-distribution inspection without importing code from an untrusted current working directory ahead of the selected artifact.
Run targeted Doctor tests and existing release-version/vendor-contract tests. No package version bump, global install, .mcpb publication, PyPI upload, tag, release, or default-branch write.
success_metrics: Stable JSON distinguishes grammar, Python package, MCP package, plugin, vendored validator, and skill versions.
Positive fixture returns pass; mismatched package/plugin, stale skill, missing MCP, missing LSP, and opt-out fixtures return specific not_ready/fail reasons without mutation.
No output contains environment secret values or DAG content.
The skill passes quick validation and its deterministic script passes repository and installed-artifact tests.

stories.title: Define the Doctor result contract and safe probes
stories.description: Implement a stable result schema and read-only probes for runtime host, distributions, plugin manifests, vendored validator, grammar, MCP/LSP entry points, auto-emit state, and database reachability metadata. Keep versions as separate named axes.

stories.title: Create the concise script-backed scholialang-doctor skill
stories.description: Use skill-creator initialization, write a small imperative SKILL.md, bundle the deterministic Doctor script, and provide generated Codex UI metadata. Do not add auxiliary documentation inside the skill.

stories.title: Pin mismatch, absence, privacy, and installed-artifact tests
stories.description: Test healthy, mismatched, stale, absent optional surface, opt-out, and hostile-CWD cases. Assert read-only behavior and redaction. Re-run existing release/version contracts.
